headline: Vireo Growth closes FLUENT deal, reaching about 74 Florida stores
dek: Vireo Growth completed its all-stock FLUENT takeover on 9 November, adding 33 Florida stores as lenders swapped about $35.7M of debt for shares.
key_points: Vireo issued 6,148,780 shares for all of FLUENT, after FLUENT lenders converted about $35.7 million of debt into equity just before closing.
The deal adds 33 dispensaries and about 117,000 sq ft of cultivation, taking Vireo to roughly 74 Florida stores and 317,000 sq ft.
FLUENT's New York and Texas businesses will be sold separately; both sales still need regulatory approval.
Lender Chicago Atlantic and its affiliates now hold about 11.7% of Vireo on an as-converted basis, up from 6.2%.
body: Vireo Growth completed its acquisition of FLUENT Corp. on 9 November, closing an all-stock deal first announced in April and making Florida the centre of its business. The transaction adds FLUENT's 33 Florida dispensaries and about 117,000 square feet of cultivation and production space to Vireo's Green Dragon chain.

The combined Florida business now has about 74 operating dispensaries and around 317,000 square feet of cultivation and manufacturing capacity, the companies said. Vireo also picks up FLUENT's operations in Buffalo, New York, while FLUENT's remaining New York and Texas licences are being sold to other buyers.
## How the deal was paid for

The takeover was carried out through a court-approved plan of arrangement under Ontario law. FLUENT's proportionate voting and exchangeable shares were first converted into common shares, each of which was then swapped for 0.002351197 of a Vireo subordinate voting share. That ratio had been adjusted to reflect Vireo's 30-for-1 share consolidation in June. In all, Vireo issued 6,148,780 shares.

Much of FLUENT's value went to its lenders rather than its old shareholders. Just before closing, FLUENT converted about $30 million of senior secured debt into equity under an agreement signed in April, and a further $5.7 million under a second agreement signed on 1 November. Those lenders then received Vireo shares, which are locked up for six months.

Chicago Atlantic and its affiliates were among the biggest beneficiaries. According to filings summarised by MyCannabis.com, the group received 3,884,062 Vireo shares through the debt conversions and exchange, raising its stake from 6.2% to about 11.7% on an as-converted basis, with no cash changing hands.
> In cannabis consolidation, the lender often ends up as the largest winner. Vireo gained a Florida footprint, and Chicago Atlantic gained a bigger slice of Vireo.
## What Vireo keeps and what it sells

The deal does not settle FLUENT's whole footprint. Etain LLC, FLUENT's New York operator, is to be sold to an unnamed third-party operator under a July agreement. Immediately before that sale, Etain will assign its Buffalo operations and the lease on its Buffalo cultivation site to Ace Heritage LLC, a Vireo-affiliated company. The New York sale needs approval from the state's Cannabis Control Board for the change of ownership.

Cansortium Texas LLC, FLUENT's Texas operator, is to be sold to Legacy Therapeutics LLC under a May agreement. Both the New York and Texas deals remain subject to regulatory approvals and other closing conditions. Until they close, the final shape of what Vireo owns outside Florida is not fixed.

FLUENT's shares were expected to be delisted from the Canadian Securities Exchange and stop trading on the OTCQB on or about 9 November, and the company plans to stop being a reporting issuer in Canada.

Vireo calls Florida one of the country's largest medical cannabis markets, and both companies run cultivation alongside their stores there, so the deal buys growing capacity as well as shelf space. Chief executive John Mazarakis said FLUENT had already made progress on operating efficiency under a budget adopted by its board, and that the combination brings greater scale and room to improve performance. Vireo will compete with larger operators such as Trulieve, which, as we reported on 6 November, has been shrinking toward a medical core.

The deal also lines up with the federal shift for medical markets. As we reported on 6 November, DEA registered more than 900 medical dispensaries last month, and Florida was among the states approved. A larger medical footprint puts Vireo in the part of the industry that the April Schedule III order covers, and where any federal tax relief would land first.

The closing also shows how cannabis consolidation is being financed in 2026. Here a struggling operator was folded into a stronger peer through a share swap, while its senior lenders converted what they are owed into stock in the buyer. FLUENT's lenders accepted shares that cannot be sold for six months, a sign they expect the combined company to be worth more than the debt they gave up.

Watch for New York's Cannabis Control Board to rule on the Etain change of ownership and the Buffalo assignment, and for Texas regulators to approve the Cansortium Texas sale. Watch Vireo's next quarterly report for the first combined Florida numbers, and the end of the lenders' six-month lock-up in May 2027, when new holders could sell.
